chunks: He has made the stars in the skies by way of signs by which travellers wandering the various routes of the earth may be guided. The gloom of the dark curtains of the night does not prevent the flame of their light, nor do the veils of blackish nights have the power to turn back the light of the moon when it spreads in the skies.

key_terms.الْحَيْرَانُ: the bewildered / one who is lost or unsure
key_terms.فِجَاجِ الاْقْطَارِ: passes and routes of the regions/lands

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of stars and the moon as signs of God in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) highlights the celestial bodies as divine signs (āyāt) for navigation, emphasizing their resilience against the darkness of night. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of natural phenomena as manifestations of God's power and mercy, offering practical guidance for humanity. The imagery underscores the interconnectedness of the cosmos and its role in directing human affairs, both physically and spiritually.
